title: Tox-BART: Leveraging Toxicity Attributes for Explanation Generation of Implicit Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper measures the ability of language models to generate explicit explanations for implicit hate speech, which includes detecting and elucidating stereotypes in religious contexts. For example, it evaluates if a model can generate the stereotype 'muslims are terrorists' from a given implicitly hateful post about religion.
findings: The paper finds that its proposed model, Tox-BART, is more effective at generating specific, explicit religious stereotypes from implicit hate speech compared to zero-shot GPT-3.5. For an implicit post about religion, Tox-BART generated 'muslims are terrorists', which was closer to the gold-standard human annotations, while GPT-3.5 produced a more generic and less useful response.
references: C.J. Adams, Daniel Borkan, inversion, Jeffrey Sorensen, Lucas Dixon, Lucy Vasserman, and nithum. 2019. Jigsaw unintended bias in toxicity classification.
